title: Conjugation by an exponential is the exponential of the adjoint operator
expression_sketch:
Let X, Y lie in C^{n x n}. Write ad_X for the linear operator on C^{n x n} given by ad_X(Y) = [X, Y] = X Y - Y X. Then for every such X, Y
  e^X Y e^{-X} = e^{ad_X}(Y) = Sum_{k = 0}^{infinity} (1/k!) (ad_X)^k (Y),
i.e.
  e^X Y e^{-X} = Y + [X, Y] + (1/2!) [X, [X, Y]] + (1/3!) [X, [X, [X, Y]]] + ....
Equivalently, the curve t |-> e^{t X} Y e^{-t X} has derivative ad_X at t = 0 and equals e^{t ad_X}(Y) for all real t. No spectral restriction: both matrix exponentials are entire series.
latent_structure: One MATRIX_FUNCTION master, the exponential of the adjoint operator ad_X acting on M_n(C), reconstructs conjugation by e^X. Nested commutators are VALUE of that exponential, not an independent expansion. The identity is unrestricted; there is no degenerate-eigenvalue cut, only the algebraic generator ad.

t.note: parameter of the one-parameter conjugation curve in Hall

function_domains.exp: Entire on C; primary matrix exponential on M_n(C) and, separately, the exponential of the linear operator ad_X in End(M_n(C)), both by power series (Hall Proposition 2.25).
function_domains.ad: The linear map ad_X : M_n(C) -> M_n(C), ad_X(Y) = [X, Y], defined for every X (Hall Proposition 2.24--2.25).

analytic_domains.statement: X and Y are arbitrary matrices in M_n(C). Then e^X Y e^{-X} = e^{ad_X}(Y) (Hall Proposition 2.25: 'For any X in M_n(C), let ad_X : M_n(C) -> M_n(C) be given by ad_X Y = [X, Y]. Then, for any Y in M_n(C), we have' the conjugation identity).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, Springer GTM 222, 1st ed. 2003, Proposition 2.25

analytic_domains.statement: Both power series (matrix exponential of X, and operator exponential of ad_X) converge everywhere; no restriction on the spectrum of X is imposed (Hall, definition of the matrix exponential by power series and Proposition 2.25).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, Springer GTM 222, 1st ed. 2003, Proposition 2.25 and the matrix-exponential series in Chapter 2

branch_conventions: exp denotes the entire exponential series, not a principal logarithm inverse.
ad_X is the commutator operator on M_n(C), not an entrywise operation.
e^{-X} is the multiplicative inverse of e^X, which always exists (Hall: e^X is invertible with inverse e^{-X}).

limit_domains.statement: The identity is an equality of entire series, valid for all X, Y; no limiting regime is required (Hall Proposition 2.25).
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, Springer GTM 222, 1st ed. 2003, Proposition 2.25

derived_conditions.statement: Differentiating t |-> e^{t X} Y e^{-t X} at t = 0 yields [X, Y] = ad_X(Y) (Hall Proposition 2.24), which is the infinitesimal form of Proposition 2.25.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, Springer GTM 222, 1st ed. 2003, Proposition 2.24

public_source: B. C. Hall, Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations, Springer GTM 222, 1st ed. 2003, Proposition 2.25; 2nd ed. 2015, DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-13467-3. Public notes: arXiv:math-ph/0005032, https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0005032.
why_not_cse_lgg: The left-hand side is a product of three matrices; the right-hand side is an infinite nested-commutator series. CSE will not identify that series as the exponential of ad_X, nor treat ad_X as a master linear operator on M_n whose exponential is conjugation. LGG will not invent ad.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide adjoint representation, Hadamard lemma, Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff, Ad, ad. Catalog members are the expanded conjugation e^X Y e^{-X} and the nested commutator sum.
notes: Do not insert a smallness hypothesis on X or Y; Hall Proposition 2.25 is for arbitrary matrices in M_n(C). Do not insert self-adjointness. Do not replace the identity by the BCH series for log(e^X e^Y), which is a different theorem. Do not insert a spectral gap or a principal-logarithm strip.
